newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul private institutes raise '97 GDP forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Seoul private institutes raise '97 GDP forecasts.

text.p: South Korea's private research centres said on Friday they had revised upward their forecasts for the country's gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year due largely to recovering exports.
Economic research institutes affiliated with the nation's major business conglomerates said GDP would expand 5.5-6.2 percent this year, compared with their earlier forecasts of 4.7-5.7 percent.
GDP grew a real 7.1 percent in 1996. In May, the Bank of Korea revised its GDP forecast to 5.5-6.0 percent this year, down from its earlier projection of 6.4 percent last November.

Samsung Economic Research Institute raised its GDP forecast to 5.8 percent this year from its March projection of 5.0 percent. "The economy is picking up faster than expected, led by recovering exports," said Hong Soon-young, a fellow at the Samsung institute.
The won's depreciation against the dollar helped boost South Korean exports and the yen's rise against the dollar was expected to boost exports from late this year, he said.
As a result, Samsung revised its forecast for the current account deficit this year down to $17 billion from its previous forecast of $20 billion.
South Korea recorded a $23.72 billion deficit in 1996.
Daewoo Research Institute said GDP would grow 5.5 percent this year, an upward revision from its forecast of 4.7 percent in March.
But Daewoo said the current account deficit would shrink slightly to $18.9 billion from its earlier projection of $19.1 billion.
"Despite a rebound in exports, high levels of inventories would hinder a fast economic recovery," said Shin Ho-shik, an economist at Daewoo institute.
LG Economic Research Institute said GDP growth would reach 6.2 percent, up from its earlier forecast of 5.7 percent.
LG said the current account deficit would be $16 billion, down from its previous projection of $16.6 billion.

Forecasts for this year's consumer price index, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, were readjusted downward to 4.2-4.7 percent from earlier forecasts of 4.3-5.0 percent, the private institutes said.
